# Getting an image {#sec-getting-an-image}

This chapter gives one recipe for each kind of image you can take by hand:
a still image, a bioluminescence image, a composite, a video and a Z-stack.
The controls each recipe uses are described in @sec-channels and
@sec-focus, and the toolbar's buttons in @sec-toolbar. To take images
automatically, at many positions or over time, use a protocol.

## Before you start {#sec-image-before}

- Place the sample in its labware holder (@sec-labware-holders), seated
  flat.
- Make sure LumaViewPro knows which objective is in the light path
  (@sec-objective). Until it does, captures are refused.
- Choose the destination folder with the toolbar's Destination folder
  button. Every image and video you take is saved under it
  (@sec-image-files).
- Choose the file format in [Live Image Format]{.guilabel} (@sec-live-format)
  and the bit depth in [Image Mode]{.guilabel}
  (@sec-image-mode), both in [Microscope Settings]{.guilabel}.

## A still image {#sec-image-still}

For a transmitted-light or fluorescence channel:

1. On a Lumascope with a motorized XY stage, move to the sample, or to the
   first well of a plate: click the point on the plate map in
   [XY Stage Control]{.guilabel} (@sec-plate-map).
2. Open the channel's drawer in the right panel, for example
   [Brightfield]{.channel}. The live image shows that channel.
3. Switch on [Enable LED]{.guilabel} to light the channel's LED.
4. Adjust the focus until the sample is sharp (@sec-focus-adjust), or use
   [Autofocus]{.guilabel} once the image is near focus (@sec-autofocus).
5. Adjust [LED (mA)]{.guilabel}, [Gain (dB)]{.guilabel} and
   [Exp (ms)]{.guilabel} until the image is bright without being
   saturated: the histogram (@sec-histogram) should have most of its
   pixels away from either end.
6. On a Lumascope with a focus motor, click [Save Focus]{.guilabel} to save
   this focus for the channel (@sec-channel-focus). To come back to this
   place later, click [Set Z]{.guilabel} in [Objective Control]{.guilabel}
   and, on a Lumascope with a motorized XY stage, [Set X]{.guilabel} and
   [Set Y]{.guilabel} in [XY Stage Control]{.guilabel}.
7. Click the toolbar's Capture button.

The image is saved in the `Manual` folder of the destination folder, named
for the channel shown, with a number that counts up with each capture, for
example `live_BF_000001.tiff`. On a Lumascope with a motorized XY stage, the
name also gives the well the image was taken in, as in
`live_D6_BF_000001.tiff`. A TIFF or OME-TIFF file records the channel, the
LED current, the gain, the exposure, the objective and the stage position;
a JPG records none of them (@sec-live-format).

Capture saves whatever the camera delivers. An image taken with the LED
switched off is saved, dark; check [Enable LED]{.guilabel} first. The
Freeze button stops only the display: Capture still saves a new image from
the camera, not the frozen picture.

If the stage position is not known, for example before the stage has
homed, the image is saved without a well or a position, and LumaViewPro
says so ("Position Not Recorded"). Click [Home Stage]{.guilabel} to record
them in later images.

Right-click a point of the live image to center it before you
capture (@sec-click-to-center).

## A bioluminescence image {#sec-image-lumi}

Requires: the [Lumi]{.channel} channel.

A luminescent sample is often too faint to focus in its own light. Focus
in a transmitted channel first:

1. Open the [Brightfield]{.channel} or [Phase Contrast]{.channel} drawer,
   switch on [Enable LED]{.guilabel}, focus on the sample, and click
   [Save Focus]{.guilabel}.
2. Open the [Lumi]{.channel} drawer. It has no LED; the camera images the
   light the sample emits.
3. Raise [Gain (dB)]{.guilabel} and [Exp (ms)]{.guilabel} toward the top
   of their ranges.
4. If the live image still shows nothing, set [Sum]{.guilabel} to add
   several frames into each image, for example 4 (@sec-sum). Summing
   keeps its added range only in a full-depth [Image Mode]{.guilabel}.
5. Click the toolbar's Capture button, then open the image with the
   toolbar's Open last save folder button and check that the
   luminescence shows.

To image the [Lumi]{.channel} channel at the focus found in transmitted
light, save that same focus in the [Lumi]{.channel} drawer with
[Save Focus]{.guilabel} while the focus is unchanged.

## A composite image {#sec-image-composite}

A composite combines several channels of the same field into one image:
fluorescence channels over each other, or over one transmitted channel.

1. Set up and focus each channel as for a still image, and in each
   channel's drawer set [Acquire Settings]{.guilabel} to
   [Image]{.guilabel} (@sec-channel-acquire). At least two channels must
   be set to [Image]{.guilabel}; with fewer, the composite is refused
   ("Not Enough Channels").
2. For each fluorescence or [Lumi]{.channel} channel, set
   [CBT (%)]{.guilabel}, the brightness above which its pixels are laid
   over the transmitted image (@sec-cbt).
3. Click the toolbar's Composite button. Each channel is captured in turn
   with its own settings, at its saved focus (or at the current focus, for
   a channel with no saved focus), and with an autofocus first if its
   [Auto Focus]{.guilabel} is on. Click Composite again to stop.

Each composite is saved in a new folder, `Manual/Composites/<date>_<time>/`
in the destination folder: one image per channel, for example
`Composite_BF_0000.tiff`, and the combined image in its `Composite`
folder. Composites are saved as TIFF or OME-TIFF
(@sec-sequenced-format). The per-channel images keep the bit depth of the
[Image Mode]{.guilabel} (@sec-image-mode); the combined image is 8-bit
color.

## A video {#sec-image-video}

1. Set up and focus the channel as for a still image.
2. Click the toolbar's Record button. Click it again to stop; otherwise
   the recording stops at [Video Time Limit (s)]{.guilabel}, 300 seconds
   unless changed in [Advanced Settings]{.guilabel} (@sec-advanced-camera).

The video is saved in the `Manual` folder, named for the date and time it
started, for example `Video_2026-11-04_21.28.29.mp4`. Its name does not
give the channel; a file beside it, ending in `_manifest.json`, records
the channel and the frames written. With [Video Recording Format]{.guilabel}
set to [Frames]{.guilabel}, the frames are saved as separate images in a
folder of the same name instead (@sec-video-format).

A recording cannot be started while a protocol runs, and the destination
folder and the objective cannot be changed while it records.

## A Z-stack {#sec-image-zstack}

Requires: a focus motor.

1. Set up the channel as for a still image, and focus at the depth you
   want as the stack's top, center or bottom.
2. In [Objective Control]{.guilabel}, under [Acquire Z Stack]{.guilabel},
   set the step size, the range and where the stack sits against the
   current focus (@sec-zstack).
3. Click [Acquire]{.guilabel}.

The slices are saved in a new folder, `Manual/Z-Stacks/<date>_<time>/`.

## Where the files are saved {#sec-image-files}

Everything is saved under the destination folder. Each folder is made the
first time something is saved in it.

| Folder | What it holds |
|:---|:---|
| `Manual` | Still images and videos taken with Capture and Record. |
| `Manual/Composites/<date>_<time>` | One folder for each composite. |
| `Manual/Z-Stacks/<date>_<time>` | One folder for each Z-stack. |
| `ProtocolData/<date>_<time>` | One folder for each protocol run. |

: The folders under the destination folder {#tbl-image-folders tbl-colwidths="[40,60]"}

With [Save channels in separate folders]{.guilabel} on in
[Advanced Settings]{.guilabel} (@sec-advanced-protocol), still images are
saved in a folder for each channel inside `Manual`, for example
`Manual/BF`.

The toolbar's Open last save folder button opens the folder LumaViewPro
last saved to.
